review_items.rationale: The answering artifact is b5382a9e45384354ae2bb134e74ae95b version 1, executed as b617d2d55bac4add81288c1f82e19cd0; its fixed plan/harness and claim C_append_completed_quorum version 1 were inspected together. The documented duty in S_append_duty is persistence before counting entries toward commitment; S_async_contract assigns append completion before attached-response delivery to the caller. The fixed three-voter majority, with no outgoing voters, follows S_joint/S_majority. This supports the one-way commitment-implies-completed-majority obligation, not an equality or a deadline for commitment. RawNode, rather than Node, is the selected API. The harness serializes calls on one goroutine, constructs empty stores, Bootstraps actual peers, campaigns node 1, and processes actual Ready/local responses to reach a stored, committed and applied prefix at index 4. It then Proposes the actual payload at index 5, term 2. No critical raft or tracker fields are assigned. Append work is FIFO and retained while blocked; each processed message performs MemoryStorage.Append and any SetHardState before releasing its actual Responses. Apply work uses actual MsgStorageApply entries and applies bootstrap configuration entries through ApplyConfChange. No Advance is called in async mode. These inputs establish one legal no-crash modeled-storage history, not disconnected fragments. The four phase_admitted records precede distinct quorum_observed records, correlated by the independent request/phase pair. Index 5 and term 2 remain identical throughout. prefix_complete and proposal_accepted are emitted only after the corresponding runtime checks and successful calls; result fields are not used as prerequisites or applicability filters. The result computes committed from the implementation commit index, and append_completed_majority from separate per-voter MemoryStorage reads matching target term and payload. Match is diagnostic only, so the oracle does not assume the fact being tested. The actual observations are: stored copies 0,1,2,3; commit indexes 4,4,5,5; leader Match 4,4,4,5; leader application 4,4,4,5. At the two-follower checkpoint storage_last=[4,5,5] and Match=[4,5,5] distinguish a valid remote majority from leader-local persistence. The fixed scheduler terminates on exhaustion of permitted work rather than waiting for a comparison to pass, and all four comparisons plus history_finished were emitted. The parser reports no errors, no missing results, and per-result admission matches at indices 38/42/47/60 for results 41/46/59/67. Thus the bounded holds measurement corresponds to the stated necessity condition; the remote-majority phase also supplies an observed permitted path, not an inferred general sufficiency theorem.
